cands.bio: Montgomery attorney and Republican candidate for Alabama House District 74. According to his campaign site, he was a deputy district attorney in Montgomery County and an executive assistant in the governor's office. He led the State Health Planning and Development Agency from 1997 to 2018, then worked in business development at Bernhard Energy.
cands.gaps: We could not find where he was born or when he moved to Montgomery. His site says he worked "in the State House" but doesn't say in what role, and we could not confirm it. We found no record of elected office or legislative service, no independent news coverage of him, and no endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and his site says nothing on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. All biographical details come from his own campaign site and could not be checked against independent sources.

cands.bio: Democrat elected to the Alabama House of Representatives, District 74 (Montgomery), in November 2026. Her campaign site says she has spent her career working with abuse victims, sexual assault survivors and families affected by domestic violence.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by Tabitha's List (a Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (a Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where she was born or raised, or when she moved to Alabama. We couldn't verify her employer, job titles or years of work, or whether she has held any prior office. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and her campaign site lists only broad themes (public education, healthcare access, infrastructure and mobility, safer neighborhoods) with no specific positions. We found no stated positions or actions from her on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, policing or school choice.
